successors.name: Principality of Anhalt
successors.text: the Anhalt lands: Bernburg, Kothen, Dessau and Zerbst

successors.name: Duchy of Saxe-Lauenburg
successors.text: the land around Ratzeburg and Lauenburg

ledger.x: 1260: after the death of Albert I of Saxony his sons John I and Albert II rule the Ascanian lands jointly.
20 September 1296: the Duchy of Saxony is partitioned into Saxe-Wittenberg and Saxe-Lauenburg.
1307: the Askanier acquire the lordship of Zerbst from the lords of Barby (paraphrased; the page gives the year, not the extent of the lordship).
1315: the Aschersleben line dies out and its district passes to the Bishopric of Halberstadt, splitting Anhalt-Bernburg in two (Principality of Anhalt: 'annexed by the Bishopric of Halberstadt').
25 April 1344: the counts of Weimar-Orlamunde sell Orlamunde to the Wettins: 'Orlamünde was sold to the Wettins on April 25, 1344.'

1356: the Golden Bull gives Rudolph I of Saxe-Wittenberg the Saxon electoral dignity (he 'exclusively received the Saxon electoral dignity'); Saxe-Wittenberg then came to be known as the Electorate of Saxony.
1363: the Ascanian electorate of Saxe-Wittenberg passes to Cliopatria's Electorate of Saxony row (starts 1363; the page dates the dignity to 1356).
1370: 'In the same year, the Principality of Lüneburg was granted to Albrecht and Wenceslaus I' of the Saxe-Wittenberg line (House of Ascania; its table: 'Luneburg (until 1388)').
1372: Herman VI, the last count of Weimar of the line, dies and the Wettins annex Weimar: 'After Herman's death Weimar was annexed to the House of Wettin.'
1388: 'The Ascanians were replaced in 1388 by Albrecht's stepsons from the House of Welf' (House of Ascania).

1468: 'The last prince of the original line of Anhalt-Bernburg died in 1468' and 'his lands were inherited by the princes of the sole remaining line, that of Anhalt-Zerbst' (Principality of Anhalt prose; the page's table says instead that 'Bernburg was inherited by Anhalt-Dessau line', and the page has George I…
1473: after Adolph's death Valdemar VI and Albert VI of the Dessau line take over Kothen under the succession contract of 1471 (paraphrased).
1486: Cliopatria's House of Ascania row ends.

wars.name: Luneburg succession (Ascanians against the Welfs)
wars.outcome: The Ascanians are enfeoffed with Luneburg (1369-1370), the towns pay homage (January 1371), the Reconciliation of Hanover (1373) sets alternating rule, and Henry's victory at Winsen (28 May 1388) and the inheritance agreement of 1389 secure the principality…

certainty.note: Scattered principalities and counties of one house; no page opened gives a surveyed line.
